transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, thank you. Um… I guess what brings me in is this restless feeling I’ve been having. It’s not, you know, dramatic or anything, but I feel kind of wound too tight a lot of the time, like I can’t fully settle. Even when I’m just supposed to be sitting through a planning meeting, or doing something calm like painting or yoga, I still feel like I’m sort of buzzing inside. If that makes sense.
Do you ever have sudden surges of intense fear or discomfort that peak within minutes?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I can get uncomfortable or worked up sometimes, but not like a sudden wave of intense fear that peaks really fast. At least, I haven’t noticed anything like that. Does that make sense?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different parts of your life?

I don’t think I worry a lot across everything, no. I mean, I have normal concerns like anyone, work or family stuff, but it doesn’t feel like my main issue is worry, if that’s the right way to put it. I’m not sure if I’m answering that clearly.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually high, euphoric, or unusually irritable?

I don’t think I’ve had anything like that, no. I mean, I can get irritable sometimes, sure, but not in a way that feels unusually high or euphoric or like a big shift from my normal self. At least not that I’ve recognized. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often have trouble staying focused on tasks or conversations, even when you want to pay attention?

Yes, sometimes. I don’t want to overstate it, but it does happen. Like in sourcing meetings, or even at dinner, I can be looking right at someone while they’re asking me something, and then a few seconds later I realize I only really caught the last part. Then I have to ask them to repeat it, which is embarrassing. I am trying to pay attention, it’s not that I don’t care. Does that count as what you mean?
Looking back, were these focus problems already present when you were a child?

Yes, I think so. I mean, I wasn’t a “bad kid” or anything, but I do remember in elementary school getting notes sent home because I’d pop out of my seat, talk over other kids, or blurt out an answer before the teacher had even finished asking the question. I guess at the time people just saw it as me being energetic or impatient. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Do these focus or restlessness problems interfere with your work or relationships?

Yes… I mean, not terribly, I don’t think, but it does get in the way sometimes. At work, I’ve had purchase orders that needed corrections, and my planning coordinator has had to give them an extra look, which is embarrassing because I do care about doing things properly.

And at home, I think family dinners can get a little tense because people feel like I’m talking over them. I don’t mean to, but I can see how it comes across that way. Is that the kind of interference you mean?
Have you been feeling down or depressed much of the time lately?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I have frustrating days and I can get embarrassed about mistakes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling depressed most of the time. At least, not that I’ve noticed.
